reports.title: Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información (ONEI)
reports.publisher: Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información
reports.description: Cuba's national statistics and information office; compiles the annual Anuario Estadístico de Cuba statistical yearbook, including a national-accounts (Cuentas Nacionales) chapter and price data. Cuba withdrew from the IMF in 1964 and is not a Fund member, so — unlike every other country in this batch — it does not participate in any IMF data-dissemination tier (e-GDDS/SDDS/SDDS Plus).

reports.title: Oficina Nacional de Estadística (ONE)
reports.description: The Dominican Republic's national statistics office, coordinating the national statistical system (censuses, surveys, classifications); national accounts and CPI compilation are carried out separately by the Banco Central de la República Dominicana.

reports.title: Banco Central de la República Dominicana (BCRD)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de la República Dominicana
reports.description: The Dominican Republic's central bank. Its National Accounts and Economic Statistics Department compiles and disseminates the country's national accounts and Consumer Price Index, and it hosts the country's IMF e-GDDS National Summary Data Page.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales de la República Dominicana (National Accounts)
reports.publisher: Banco Central de la República Dominicana
reports.description: Official national accounts / GDP estimates for the Dominican Republic, compiled quarterly and annually by BCRD's National Accounts and Economic Statistics Department using accrual-basis accounting and ISIC Rev.4 / CPC Version 2 classifications.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) — Dominican Republic
reports.publisher: Banco Central de la República Dominicana
reports.description: Official monthly Dominican Republic Consumer Price Index, covering 305 items in 12 COICOP groups, based on the 2007-08 national household income/expenditure survey (ENIGH).

reports.title: Institut Haïtien de Statistique et d'Informatique (IHSI)
reports.publisher: Institut Haïtien de Statistique et d'Informatique
reports.description: Haiti's national statistics institute. Its statistical system is under real, verifiable strain: the institute's own domain (ihsi.ht) currently 302-redirects away from any IHSI content, and the only located IMF DQAF metadata on Haiti's CPI/national-accounts methodology is an unrefreshed, internally inconsistent GDDS-era entry (constant-price base year 1986/87; CPI base August 2004).

reports.title: Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN)
reports.description: Jamaica's national statistical institute, responsible for national accounts, CPI, censuses and surveys, and the country's IMF e-GDDS National Summary Data Page.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) — Jamaica
reports.description: Official monthly Jamaican CPI covering about 85% of households via roughly 49,700 monthly price quotations across all parishes; Laspeyres formula, base period December 2006=100.

reports.title: Jamaica National Income and Product / National Accounts
reports.description: Official Jamaican national accounts / GDP estimates, released quarterly and annually. STATIN announced completion of the transition from the 1993 SNA to the 2008 SNA framework in July 2025.

reports.title: Central Statistical Office (CSO), Trinidad and Tobago
reports.description: Trinidad and Tobago's national statistical office, under the Ministry of Planning, Economic Affairs and Development; responsible for national accounts, the retail price index (CPI), and the country's e-GDDS National Summary Data Page (coordinated with the Central Bank and Ministry of Finance).

reports.title: Index of Retail Prices (Consumer Price Index) — Trinidad and Tobago
reports.description: Official monthly Trinidad and Tobago retail/consumer price index; Modified Laspeyres formula, weights from the 2008/2009 Household Budget Survey, base period January 2015=100.

reports.title: National Accounts / Gross Domestic Product — Trinidad and Tobago
reports.description: Official Trinidad and Tobago national accounts/GDP estimates (annual and quarterly, by economic activity), at current and constant 2012 prices, production-approach based.

reports.title: Bahamas National Statistical Institute (BNSI)
reports.description: The Bahamas' national statistics agency; established in 1968 as the Department of Statistics and officially renamed/restructured as the BNSI under the Statistics Act, March 2021. Responsible for CPI, national accounts, census data and the country's e-GDDS National Summary Data Page.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) — Bahamas
reports.description: Official monthly Bahamian CPI covering New Providence and Grand Bahama, weighted from the 2013/2014 Household Budgetary Survey across 12 expenditure categories.

reports.title: National Accounts / Gross Domestic Product — Bahamas
reports.description: Official Bahamian national accounts/GDP estimates (quarterly and annual), production and expenditure approaches, base year 2012, ISIC Rev.4 industry classification.

reports.title: Barbados Statistical Service
reports.description: Barbados' national statistics office; produces annual national-accounts estimates at current prices and the retail price index. The Central Bank of Barbados separately produces quarterly/constant-price GDP estimates (most recently rebased to a 2023 base year with IMF Statistics Department and CARTAC technical assistance).

reports.title: Retail Price Index (CPI) — Barbados
reports.description: Official Barbadian retail/consumer price index, compiled from a c.340-item basket drawn from the 1998/99 household budget survey.

reports.title: Statistics Division, Antigua and Barbuda
reports.publisher: Statistics Division, Ministry of Finance and Corporate Governance
reports.description: Antigua and Barbuda's national statistics office; compiles national accounts jointly with the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank. Its own site (statistics.gov.ag) could not be independently loaded during this research pass (TLS/certificate error on fetch); this node's existence and methodology are corroborated instead via the IMF's own DSBB metadata for Antigua and Barbuda.

reports.title: Central Statistical Office, Saint Lucia
reports.description: Saint Lucia's national statistics office; produces annual GDP estimates via production and expenditure approaches, plus labour, inflation, tourism and census statistics.

reports.title: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB)
reports.description: Regional central bank for the eight-member Eastern Caribbean Currency Union — Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines — publishing national accounts, monetary, fiscal and external-sector statistics for its member territories, with national accounts compiled jointly with each territory's own statistics office.

reports.title: System of National Accounts, 1968 (1968 SNA)
reports.description: The 1968 edition of the UN System of National Accounts. Superseded internationally by the 1993 and 2008 editions, but still the explicitly named governing framework in current IMF DQAF metadata for some smaller economies' national-accounts compilation.

reports.title: Caribbean Community (CARICOM)
reports.description: Regional integration organisation of 15 member states and 8 associate members, established 4 July 1973 by the Treaty of Chaguaramas (signed by Barbados, Guyana, Jamaica and Trinidad and Tobago); coordinates economic integration, foreign policy and functional cooperation across the Caribbean. Added 2026-08-25 as the generic CARICOM-institution node, distinct from gy-caricom (Guyana's own country-specific CARICOM-membership record) — see HANDOFF.md §5 item 5b.

dependencies.basis: The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for the Dominican Republic's national-accounts category states the current methodology explicitly, ending {"The national accounts are currently estimated with a methodology based on the concepts and definitions of the System of National Accounts, 2008 (2008 SNA)"}.

The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for the Dominican Republic's CPI category states the concepts used follow {"the definitions of the International Labour Organization (ILO) and the 2004 Consumer Price Index Manual of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)"}.

The IMF's own press release announcing the country's participation is titled {"The Dominican Republic Implements the International Monetary Fund's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System"}, dated February 22, 2019; BCRD separately hosts the country's National Summary Data Page.
The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for Jamaica's CPI category states the data {"are consistent with the concepts and definitions of the Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice (2004)"}.

The Jamaica Information Service (the government's own news service) reported STATIN's Acting Director General announcing the national accounts revision, stating it involved {"aligning the national accounts with the United Nations System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)"}.

Jamaica's IMF DSBB metadata pages are filed under the e-GDDS URL path ("egdds/dqaf-base/country/JAM/...") and returned live DQAF content for Jamaica's CPI, national-accounts and government-operations categories, confirming e-GDDS participation and an IMF-facing National Summary Data Page, e.g. {"The classification system used for the CPI is the Classification of Individual Consumption according to Purpose (COICOP) Version 2.0"} from Jamaica's e-GDDS DQAF entry.

The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for Trinidad and Tobago's national-accounts category states {"The National Accounts for Trinidad and Tobago are broadly consistent with the System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)"}.

The Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's own e-GDDS page states {"The Government of Trinidad and Tobago has subscribed to the IMF's Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS)"}, naming the Central Bank, Ministry of Finance and Central Statistical Office as joint implementers.

The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for the Bahamas' national-accounts category states {"Compilation is based on '2008 SNA', using both production and expenditure approaches with 2012 as the base year for constant price series"}.

The Central Bank of the Bahamas' own e-GDDS page states {"Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund's DSBB"} and hosts the national accounts, CPI, government-operations, monetary and balance-of-payments datasets that make up the country's e-GDDS National Summary Data Page.

Barbados' IMF DSBB DQAF pages are filed under the e-GDDS URL path (e.g. "dsbb.imf.org/e-gdds/dqaf-base/country/BRB/category/IND00") and the API behind those pages returns live Barbados-specific national-accounts and CPI methodology content, confirming e-GDDS-tier participation.

The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for Antigua and Barbuda's national-accounts category names the governing framework as {"System of National Accounts 1968" (1968 SNA)} and states compilation is a joint effort of "Antigua and Barbuda's Statistics Division and the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank."

The IMF DSBB's DQAF summary for Saint Lucia's national-accounts category states national accounts are based on {"System of National Accounts 1968" (1968 SNA)}, with described adjustments toward select 1993 SNA treatments (FISIM, mineral exploration, software capitalization) that fall short of a full edition change.
CARICOM's own member-state directory lists Jamaica's own country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 1 Aug 1973"}.

CARICOM's own member-state directory lists Trinidad and Tobago's country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 1 Aug 1973"}; the CSO's own site independently lists CARICOM as an affiliate organisation.
CARICOM's own member-state directory lists the Bahamas' country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 4 Jul 1983"}.
CARICOM's own member-state directory lists Barbados' country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 1 Aug 1973"}.
CARICOM's own member-state directory lists Haiti's country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 1 Jul 2002"}.
CARICOM's own member-state directory lists Antigua and Barbuda's country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 4 Jul 1974"}.
CARICOM's own member-state directory lists Saint Lucia's country profile page, which states {"Date of Membership in CARICOM: 1 May 1974"}.

_dropped.why: [EDITION-AMBIGUOUS] Jamaica's DSBB DQAF entry names the classification as "COICOP Version 2.0", which is DSBB/IMF-internal versioning language, not a clean match to either the corpus's un-coicop-hbs-1999 or un-coicop-2018 node (neither year/edition is stated). Grok's batch2 proposed wiring this to un-coicop-hbs-1999 on the reasoning that "Version 2.0" corresponds to the 1999/2004-era framework — that is plausible-sounding inference, not something the document itself states, so per the edition-matching rule it is dropped rather than guessed.

[SUPERSEDED] Grok's batch2 proposal (and STATIN's own older nas.pdf concepts document, and Jamaica's DSBB DQAF national-accounts entry) explicitly state Jamaica compiles under the 1993 SNA. However, a July 2025 Jamaica Information Service (government news service) article quotes STATIN's own Acting Director General announcing the transition to 2008 SNA is complete. The 1993 SNA statement is real but now outdated; sna-2008 was minted instead using the more current source. sna-1993 does not currently exist in the corpus and was not proposed as a new node here since the country-specific edge for it is superseded.

[NO-EDITION-STATED] Trinidad and Tobago's DSBB DQAF CPI entry states only "The Classification System used is COICOP - Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose" with no version or year given. Not enough to pick between the corpus's split COICOP-edition nodes.

[NO-EDITION-STATED] The Dominican Republic's DSBB DQAF CPI entry describes "305 items and 12 groups of products classified by purpose according to the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP)" with no edition/year named.

Neither the Bahamas' own BNSI CPI page nor the DSBB DQAF CPI00 entry for BHS references the CPI Manual or names a COICOP version — the DQAF entry describes only a 12-category expenditure framework with no international-standard citation attached.
Barbados' DSBB DQAF CPI00 entry describes the index formula, sample and base period in detail but does not reference the CPI Manual or name a COICOP version anywhere in the retrieved content.

[CONFLICTING/STALE] Barbados' DSBB DQAF national-accounts entry explicitly states "The Barbadian national accounts are based on the United Nations standard System of National Accounts of 1968 (SNA 68)" — but that same DQAF entry uses a base year (1974) and CPI-adjacent metadata that predate the Statistical Service's own 2018 CPI rebase, suggesting the whole DQAF page is stale. A 2024 Central Bank of Barbados press release on rebasing Barbados' GDP to a 2023 base year references only "internationally recommended guidelines under the System of National Accounts" with no edition named. Given one source is explicit-but-likely-outdated and the other is current-but-vague, no edition can be confidently minted; this is a real methodology dependency with the target genuinely unclear, exactly the wrong-target case the schema describes.

Grok's batch1 proposed this edge with a placeholder, non-quoted "evidence_quote" reading "CARICOM membership and statistical cooperation framework (reused target as instructed)" — not a real quote from any page. CARICOM's own official member-state directory (fetched live) lists exactly 15 Member States and 8 Associate Members and explicitly does NOT include the Dominican Republic in either list; the DR has a bilateral free-trade arrangement with CARICOM but is not a member or associate member. Dropped as denied rather than minted.

[CUBA IMF STATUS — per PROMPT.md's explicit instruction to check rather than assume] Cuba withdrew from IMF membership in 1964 and remains a non-member (widely and consistently corroborated; the IMF's own imf.org/en/countries/cub page 404s, consistent with no active member profile). Non-members do not participate in DSBB/e-GDDS/SDDS/SDDS Plus, so no dissemination-tier edge exists to mint for Cuba, unlike every other country in this batch.

_dropped.why: onei.gob.cu (both the main site and every specific PDF publication URL located, including the 2022-2024 Anuario Estadístico national-accounts chapters) returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED / robots.txt-fetch-failure to automated fetching throughout this research pass, and no independent mirror or secondary primary source with a Cuba-specific SNA/COICOP methodology quote could be located. cu-onei is still minted as an institutional node (its real-world existence and publication activity are corroborated by numerous distinct, specifically-named document URLs turned up in search, e.g. "05-cuentas-nacionales_aec2024.pdf"), but no specific methodology claim about it could be independently verified this round.

[INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT, STALE] Haiti's DSBB DQAF national-accounts entry states "National accounts are prepared in accordance with SNA 1968 methodology. SNA 1993 has not yet been implemented," while the separate DQAF CPI entry for Haiti states in the same metadata set that "Prices and weights of CPI follow the concepts of national accounts (SNA 1993)." The two categories of the same DQAF filing contradict each other on the edition, both use decades-old base periods (constant-price base 1986/87; CPI base August 2004), and Haiti's institutional capacity has been substantially disrupted since this metadata was last plausibly current. Per the honesty-permission and evidence-standard rules, this is recorded as a genuine but unresolvable ambiguity rather than minted.

Old DQAF category pages for HTI do exist in the DSBB system (implying historical GDDS-era filing), but no current statement of Haiti's active e-GDDS/NSDP status could be located, and IHSI's own domain (ihsi.ht) currently 302-redirects to an unrelated third-party site rather than resolving to any IHSI content — itself evidence against an actively maintained National Summary Data Page. Consistent with the brief's expectation that Haiti would come back thin.
Haiti's DQAF CPI entry mentions "COICOP (Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose), which is consistent with international standards" with no version/year given.
